title: The pilgrimage that never ended
text: {{1}} over a thousand years, Christians have walked across northern Spain to {{2}} shrine of St James at Santiago de Compostela. {{3}} was never simply a long hike: medieval walkers believed the journey reduced their time in purgatory, and the route {{4}} never quite lost its grip. {{5}} draws today's crowds — well over 400,000 a year — is not only faith {{6}} also the promise of headspace, friendship and a landscape that changes hourly. The Camino owes {{7}} modern boom partly to guidebooks, films and a holy year in 2010, {{8}} numbers passed 270,000 for the first time. The scallop shell, once a badge of medieval penitents, is now more likely to hang from a backpack than from a staff.

gaps.explanation: Durations take 'for': for over a thousand years.

gaps.hint: article: to ___ shrine of St James
gaps.explanation: A specific, identified shrine takes the definite article.

gaps.hint: pronoun: ___ was never simply a hike
gaps.explanation: 'It' refers to the walk as the subject.

gaps.hint: auxiliary: the route ___ never quite lost
gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has lost.
Fused relative subject: what draws them.

gaps.hint: conjunction: not only faith ___ also headspace
gaps.explanation: 'Not only … but also' — the fixed pair.
The boom belongs to the route: its boom.
Non-defining time clause after the year.
